topic: K Framework executable semantics, regression testing, and reachability claims

source.title: K User Manual
source.method: Two generic public web searches; opened one primary source page (GitHub-rendered official K User Manual). No repository content was sent to the web.
source.authority: Primary project documentation maintained in the official Runtime Verification K repository; the manual labels itself under construction, so feature guidance may be incomplete.
locators: Lines 207-214: K specifications described as executable, configuration-based, and rewrite-based.
Lines 323-332: krun executes K terms and kprove checks claims; execution process.
Lines 674-683: status-code exit cell and nonzero-by-default test-harness pattern.
Lines 1323-1328: distinction between one-path and all-path reachability claims.
Lines 347-349: backend-specific semantic modules complicate trust, even with testing.
falsifiable_source_claims: The manual states that K specs compile into runnable and testable programs and represent state as cells with rewrite rules defining transitions (lines 207-214).
The manual documents a status-code cell whose default value is 1 and says a test harness can set it to 0 only on success (lines 674-683).
The manual says Haskell backend reachability claims can be annotated all-path or one-path, and describes all-path as stronger because it considers all paths (lines 1323-1328, 1414-1419).

proposal: For Sherlock, add a per-transition QA record that captures the full pre-state, independent expected post-state, actual post-state, effects, prefix/step count, and explicit success status. Compare complete structures; classify stuck, timeout, or incomplete output as failure. Use bounded one-step examples and separate all-branch checks where branching is present.
limitation: The manual is under construction and does not specify a cross-implementation equivalence workflow. A bounded test suite cannot establish unbounded semantic equivalence.
